title: Medora prescription refill flow
brief: Medora Health wants an architecture page for how a prescription refill request travels from the patient app to the pharmacy, for the integrations team, version dated 2026-09-30. Section "Refill sequence" with four parties, named exactly: Patient App, Refill Service, Clinic EHR, Pharmacy Portal. In order: Patient App tells Refill Service "request refill"; Refill Service asks Clinic EHR "check active prescription and refills left"; Clinic EHR answers Refill Service "approved, 2 refills remaining"; Refill Service sends Pharmacy Portal "e-prescription, NCPDP SCRIPT"; Pharmacy Portal answers Refill Service "accepted, ready in 2 hours"; Refill Service tells Patient App "refill confirmed". Then show the alternative when the clinic declines: Clinic EHR answers Refill Service "denied, visit needed" and Refill Service tells Patient App "book a visit". Section "Service targets", one row per call with its target: the EHR check within 3 s; the pharmacy acknowledgement within 30 s; the confirmation shown in the app within 10 s of the request. Section "Rules" with three points: controlled substances are never refilled through the app, a refill covers at most a 90-day supply, and requests made after 21:00 wait in a queue until 07:00. Pharmacists and clinic staff will read this on their phones, so make the controlled-substance rule impossible to miss.

edit.request: The pharmacy acknowledgement target is now 45 s instead of 30 s, and the overnight queue now holds requests made after 22:00 instead of 21:00.
